title: A first herbal OCR scan comparison finds 19 word edits in 30 words; validate across pages and transcribers
statement: Pilot toward P-J-029, not its requested full validation: I compared the first four printed prose lines under ALTEA on PDF page 21 (https://archive.org/download/CAT31000255/cat31000255.pdf, page 21) with page 21 of the companion OCR. The page was chosen before viewing as an early body page; it is a convenience sample, not a random or representative sample. One reader, no independent second transcript, expanded the printed c-with-macron to cum, joined words hyphenated at printed line endings, rendered the long s as s, mapped ae/ligature to ae, and ignored marginalia and headings. After mapping ampersands to et and applying vs.refcorpus.normalize(..., 'latin'), the human line sequence is: 'altea calida et sicca cum equalitate opatio et proprietas ipsius est lenificare et maturare et mollificare et resoluere et abstergere semen et radix sunt maioris efficaciae notanter radix uiridis decoctio'. The matching OCR lines normalize to: 'altea calida et ficca cu xqualitate opatio et pro prietas ipfius eft lenificare maturare et mollifiz care et refoluere et abftergere semen et radix funt maiorisefficacia notanterradixuiridisdecoctio'. Standard Levenshtein distance on these strings is 19/204 reference characters (9.3%); on whitespace-separated tokens it is 19/30 reference words (63.3%). Long-s substitutions, a dropped conjunction, split line-end words, and fused adjacent words contribute. The comparison conflates transcription conventions and recognition errors; individual reference readings are not independently adjudicated, so the numbers are an indicative pilot, not an estimated book-wide error rate. No corrections, language-model or cipher-control tests were made. The source is public-domain and much later than the manuscript, as recorded in P-J-029.
check: Independently transcribe predefined, stratified snippets from multiple body pages with a written expansion and word-division convention; adjudicate differences and report page-level variability and uncertainty. Fit any OCR correction only on separate pages, evaluate on held-out transcripts, and compare fixed-budget cipher control recovery on corrected and reference text of matched length before adding a corpus. This pilot's result fails if its stated edit distances do not reproduce from the two provided normalized strings.
